items.text: The package returns up to the number asked for and stops when it cannot find more different valid sentences. All 1,966 were different from every other.

Each one is parsed again by the same rules that mined the text, and must have a real subject and a finite verb, with subject and verb agreement and article and noun agreement. A separate check confirms every open-class word was observed in the corpus.
8,232 sentences from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes and Pride and Prejudice, mined once, then 2,000 sentences generated with a fixed seed. One corpus, one seed.

items.claim: What the gate does not check
items.text: It checks form, not meaning. A valid sentence can still say something odd.

intro: Prose reads plain text through the rules of grammar, keeps what it learns in a HoloDb database, and recombines that knowledge into new sentences that are grammatical, use words suited to their slots and read plausibly. It exists to grow a training corpus. Mine the grammatical knowledge already in your text, which nouns, verbs and adjectives go together and how, then generate more of it, along with question and answer pairs for reading-comprehension training data.

Language models need volume and variety of grammatically correct text. Writing or scraping more does not scale, and most data augmentation either pastes fragments together ungrammatically or needs a large model of its own. Prose takes a different route. It parses real text into its grammatical structure with deterministic rules, stores what nouns, verbs and adjectives actually go with, and recombines those observed pieces into fresh sentences that are checked to parse correctly before they are written out.

why.title: Rules first, not model first
why.text: Parsing, mining and generation all run on deterministic grammar rules with no training. An optional small language model can rank candidates by plausibility, but Prose falls back to pure rules and never depends on a model to produce correct output.

why.title: No word is locked to one role
why.text: The same surface form resolves to a noun or a verb by context, the way a reader who has learned grammar reads it. In the classic example, the panda eats shoots and leaves parses as one verb with two objects, while the panda eats, shoots, and leaves parses as three verbs. Same words: the punctuation and structure alone flip the reading.

why.title: Nothing imaginary
why.text: Every open-class word Prose emits is a form it observed in the source text, and it never invents an inflection. Generated sentences are re-parsed and checked by a validity gate (a real subject, a finite verb, subject and verb agreement, article and noun agreement) before they are kept. Question and answer pairs are checked the same way on both sides.

why.title: Real grammatical structure
why.text: Beyond simple subject, verb and object sentences, Prose mines and generates indirect objects (gave him a book), relative clauses (the panda that eats bamboo) and multi-sentence passages in which later sentences refer back to earlier ones by name or pronoun, the long-context structure comprehension training needs.

diagram.title: From text to new text
diagram.stageLabel: The four stages of the Prose pipeline. Pick a sentence to parse and a generated sentence to trace.
diagram.lede: Rules parse each sentence into a subject, a verb and objects. The grammar of {sentences} sentences from {books} novels is mined into tables. New sentences are then recombined from pairs the tables contain and re-parsed by a validity gate. In a run that asked for {requested} sentences, {produced} different ones came back and every one passed the gate, with every word observed in the corpus.
diagram.caption: Run with the published EvaluatedApplications.Prose package (release {version}) on three public-domain novels from Project Gutenberg: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes and Pride and Prejudice. Every parse, count and sentence is the package's output. The generated sentences shown are the first twelve it produced with its default seed.

quickstart.lede: Mine a small block of text and generate from it. Nine sentences are enough to show the calls, but too few for the observed-pairs rule, so the output recombines freely. Mine a folder of real text and generation draws only from pairings it has seen.

also.lede: Parsing needs no mining and no database. The comma changes the parse, and the meaning with it.
The same tables produce reading-comprehension pairs: a context, a question and the answer the context supports.

For real use, mine a folder, optionally save the tables, then write a corpus and question and answer pairs to disk. This program compiles against the published package; it needs a folder of text to run.

capabilities.title: Parse
capabilities.text: Sentence splitting, part-of-speech tagging, phrase chunking and role assignment (subject, verb, objects, indirect object, predicate, relative clauses) with zero training and no external model.

capabilities.title: Mine
capabilities.text: Scans a corpus and builds a lexicon plus selectional tables: which subjects go with which verbs, which verbs take which objects and which adjectives modify which nouns. They are stored in a HoloDb database.

capabilities.title: Generate
capabilities.text: Samples a sentence shape from the mined patterns (simple, transitive, ditransitive, copular, with optional relative clauses), fills each slot with an observed, agreement-correct word, and keeps only sentences that re-parse validly.

capabilities.title: Plausibility scoring
capabilities.text: Optional. A small language model ranks generated candidates so the output reads more sensibly, without weakening the grammatical guarantee.

capabilities.title: Question and answer generation
capabilities.text: Turns generated sentences into context, question and answer triples, including multi-sentence passages with coreference and self-referential two-turn dialogues.

capabilities.title: Corpus and TSV export
capabilities.text: Write generated sentences straight to text files, or question and answer pairs to a prompt and target TSV, ready for a language model's training data.

limits: A small corpus recombines freely. Below 500 mined sentences generation falls back to the whole part-of-speech pool, so pairings need not have been seen. From 500 sentences on it draws only from pairings the tables contain.

Grammatical is not the same as meaningful. The output is built from observed pairings and checked for form, and it can still say odd things. The optional scorer ranks candidates, and correct output never depends on it.
Relative clauses are handled for subject relatives. Object relatives and non-restrictive relatives are not.
Generation is deterministic for a seed. Parallel generation uses a fixed number of shards, so it is also deterministic across machines, but it draws a different sequence from the sequential path.
It depends on HoloDb, which holds the mined tables, and on AlgFormer, which supplies the optional scorer. Installing the package brings both in.
The package ships as a binary with no source.
reference: Every public type is documented with a worked example in the package readme on NuGet.
